title: Mental Health & Wellbeing at Work
blurb: Recognising when you or a colleague are struggling, talking and listening, and where to find support, including the Samaritans.
siteNotes: Who staff can speak to at the venue about wellbeing, and how to arrange a private chat
Whether the venue has an employee assistance line or wellbeing support
Break arrangements and where staff can take them
legalNotes: From BHB-10MT-60. Employers have a duty to manage work-related stress as part of health and safety under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999.

cards.title: Mental Health & Wellbeing at Work
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- recognise signs that you or a colleague may be struggling
- talk and listen with kindness
- know where to find support

cards.title: Hospitality is demanding
cards.body:
Hospitality is a wonderful industry to work in, but it can also be demanding. Long hours, late nights, busy services and dealing with people all day can take a toll on anyone's wellbeing.

Looking after your mental health, and each other's, is just as important as physical safety.

cards.title: When you or a colleague might be struggling
cards.body:
Signs can include feeling constantly exhausted or overwhelmed, becoming withdrawn or unusually irritable, losing enthusiasm, or trouble sleeping.

> These are normal human responses to pressure, not weaknesses. Noticing them early makes them much easier to deal with.

cards.title: The most powerful thing is to talk
cards.body: If you are struggling, please speak to your manager or someone you trust. You will not be judged, and we would always rather know so we can help.

items.title: Choose someone
items.text: Your manager or someone you trust.

cards.title: Ask, then really listen
cards.body: If a colleague seems down or overloaded, a simple "are you okay?" and a genuine listen can mean the world.

left.title: Do
items: Notice a colleague who is overloaded

items.title: Samaritans
items.text: 116 123, free and confidential, day and night.

cards.title: Small habits help
cards.body: Small things help too. A team that cares about wellbeing is a stronger, happier team.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Looking after mental health matters as much as physical safety
- Struggling with pressure is human, not weakness
- Talk to your manager or someone you trust, and listen to colleagues
- Support: your manager, your GP, and Samaritans on 116 123
- Take your breaks, stay hydrated and look out for one another

cards.q: Looking after mental health is as important as physical safety.
cards.why: Looking after your mental health, and each other's, is just as important as physical safety.

cards.q: Which is a sign that you or a colleague might be struggling?
options: Asking for an extra shift to earn more
Chatting more than usual at handover
Wearing a new uniform on the shift
cards.why: Signs include constant exhaustion, feeling overwhelmed, becoming withdrawn or irritable, losing enthusiasm or trouble sleeping.

cards.q: If you are struggling, the most powerful thing to do is:
options: Bottle it up until your days off
Talk to your manager or someone you trust
cards.why: The most powerful thing any of us can do is talk, and listen.

cards.q: Struggling with pressure is a normal human response, not a weakness.
cards.why: These are normal human responses to pressure, not weaknesses.

cards.q: A colleague seems down. A good first step is to:
options: Give them space and avoid mentioning it
Ask "are you okay?" and genuinely listen
Mention it to the rest of the team
cards.why: A simple "are you okay?" and a genuine listen can mean the world.

cards.q: You would be judged for telling your manager you are struggling.
cards.why: You will not be judged, and we would always rather know so we can help.

cards.q: Which is a source of wellbeing support mentioned here?
cards.why: Support includes your manager, your GP, and free confidential helplines like the Samaritans (116 123).

cards.q: Taking your breaks and staying hydrated are small things that help.
cards.why: Small things help too: taking your breaks, staying hydrated and looking out for one another.

options: Only on weekdays in office hours
cards.why: The Samaritans are there day and night.
